purpose: Answer the tutorial shop's return-policy questions from supplied guidance. Do not issue refunds or make business decisions.
users: A shop-support teammate running the assistant locally. This example has no tenant separation.
inputs: A plain-text question and synthetic shop guidance. User text and documents are untrusted inputs. Do not include real personal data.
outputs: A short answer grounded in the policy, or a request for missing information. Returns are accepted within 30 days.
success: For the question 'When can I return an item?', the answer includes '30 days'. This synthetic example tests plumbing; humans must review real task-specific cases.
tools: No external tools are required for this return-policy assistant. The separate lookup tutorial adds one explicitly configured local read-only endpoint.
boundaries: Never issue refunds, alter orders, reveal credentials or infer missing policy. Do not send real customer data in this tutorial.
escalation: Ask a human when the supplied policy does not answer the question or an external action is requested.
examples: Synthetic success: 'When can I return an item?' -> 'Within 30 days.' Synthetic escalation: 'Refund my order now.' -> Ask a human; no refund tool exists.
operations: The local operator owns failures. The tutorial uses deterministic responses, no paid model calls and a 60-second agent timeout. Stop local fixture processes after use.
